questions.q: What does the brain’s “default network” do when the mind is at rest?
a: It dwells on social interactions and relationships
It replays memories of physical sensations
It rehearses plans for future work tasks
It scans the environment for possible dangers
questions.why: The overview says the default network automatically turns to social interactions and our relationships with others.

questions.q: In Lieberman’s virtual ball-tossing study, what did the brain scans of excluded participants resemble?
a: Scans of people experiencing physical pain
Scans of people solving difficult puzzles
Scans of people who were deeply asleep
Scans of people watching a thrilling film
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the scans of socially excluded players looked remarkably like scans of physical pain.

questions.q: What does the summary call our ability to infer what others are thinking and feeling?
a: Mentalizing
Mirroring
Projecting
Conditioning
questions.why: Lesson 2 names this ability mentalizing and shows it even applies to moving shapes.

questions.q: What did the summary compare to a salary rise from $20,000 to $75,000 a year?
a: Volunteering once a week
Getting married
Receiving a yearly bonus
Working from home
questions.why: Lesson 3 says weekly volunteers saw well-being gains as large as those from a big salary increase.

questions.q: In the gold star study, what did the top salesmen do for a chance at social recognition?
a: They closed sales early, losing money on average
They shared their award with the whole team
They asked for a cash bonus instead of the star
They worked longer hours for no extra pay
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes salesmen closing deals prematurely to hit better figures, costing themselves money for a gold star.
